(2) Upper, lower, middle (spatial relations). (3) Unity, duality, etc. (numerical relations). ALL relational concepts are empty of inherent existence — not just temporal ones.","madhyamaka":"Evaṃ krama (by the same method): the analysis of vv.1-3 generalizes universally. Śeṣau dvau (the other two divisions — past/future analyzed from present's perspective). Uttama-adhama-madhyama-ādi (upper/lower/middle etc. — spatial categories). Ekatva-ādi (unity etc. — numerical categories). All are prapañca (conceptual proliferations) that lack svabhāva.","quantum":"Gauge invariance: in physics, many \"absolute\" quantities (like voltage, position) are gauge-dependent — only RELATIVE values have physical meaning. Absolute categories (position, energy) are artifacts of the gauge choice. Like v.4: \"upper/lower,\" \"one/many\" are conventional, not absolute.","bridge":"Both gauge invariance and v.4 show that RELATIONAL concepts are conventional, not absolute. Physics: absolute position is gauge-dependent. Buddhism: \"upper/lower\" is relationally dependent. Both: only RELATIONS have meaning; absolute categories are empty constructions.","accessible":"\"Up\" and \"down\" only make sense relative to something — there's no absolute \"up\" in space. \"One\" and \"many\" depend on how you count — is a forest one thing or many trees? All categories are like this: relative, not absolute. Time is just one example.","twoTruths":"Conventionally: relational categories work — \"up,\" \"down,\" \"one,\" \"many\" function in everyday life. Ultimately: none of these exist independently — they're all relational, conventional designations. Useful but empty.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying categories are useless. \"Up\" and \"down\" WORK for building houses. \"One\" and \"many\" WORK for counting. The verse says they're not INHERENTLY real — not that they're non-functional. Convention works; inherent existence doesn't."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Gauge Invariance — Only Relations Are Physical","score":62,"strength":"Medium","explanation":"Gauge invariance: absolute quantities are gauge-dependent; only relational differences are physically meaningful. Like v.4: all categories are relational, not absolute.
